title: Build Once, Promote Everywhere 🔁
ig_caption:
Stop rebuilding—ship what you tested. 🔁

• CI builds ONE immutable artifact from the same source
• You run the full test suite against that exact artifact
• The artifact is stored (registry/artifact repo) as the deployment truth
• CD PROMOTES the same artifact to dev/stage/prod by changing only the runtime config
• No “new build” per environment → eliminates test vs shipped drift
• Key check: “0 unique builds tested ≠ shipped” becomes “shipped = tested” ✅

Production takeaway: Treat builds as immutable and promote artifacts across environments. If you must change something per env, do it via config/variables—not rebuilding.

Question: Are you confident your production binary/container is byte-for-byte identical to what your pipeline tested?
fb_caption:
Build once, promote everywhere sounds simple, but it’s an architectural reliability strategy.

What the reel highlights: 
- CI produces a single artifact and your tests validate THAT artifact.
- CD should promote the same artifact through environments (dev → staging → prod) while only adjusting environment-specific inputs (config, secrets references, feature flags, infrastructure parameters).
- This prevents “test vs shipped drift,” where rebuilding per environment leads to differences in dependencies, build args, base images, timestamps, and toolchain state.

Trade-offs and why it matters:
- Consistency: Immutable artifacts make it far more likely that what passed in staging is what runs in prod.
- Auditability: You can trace a release to a specific artifact digest/version.
- Reduced blast radius: Smaller variance lowers the probability of environment-specific regressions.
- Operational clarity: Promotion is a deliberate move of a known-good artifact, not an implicit rebuild with unknown differences.

Scalability & resilience considerations:
- Artifact registries (container registries, artifact repositories) become the system of record.
- Use immutable tags/digests and enforce promotion flows (e.g., deploy by digest, not by “latest”).
- Separate concerns: build pipeline owns compilation/packaging; deployment pipeline owns orchestration and configuration injection.

Practical best practice:
- If your pipeline rebuilds per environment, you’re reintroducing risk. Switch to artifact promotion with byte-for-byte immutability and environment-specific configuration handled separately.

What’s your biggest source of drift today—base image changes, dependency resolution, build-time env vars, or different build runners?
threads_caption: Build once, promote everywhere ✅ Stop “rebuild per env.” If prod isn’t byte-for-byte what CI tested, you don’t truly ship what you tested. What’s causing your drift: configs, base images, or build pipelines?
